column11: Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3: ‘These are the generations of Noah. Blessed be the name of the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, who chose Israel from among the seventy nations of the world, as it is written: For the portion of the Lord is His people Jacob, the lot of his inheritance (Deut. 32:9). He gave us the Written Law (the Five Books of Moses), which contains hidden and obscure teachings, and explained them in the Oral Law (codified in the Mishnah), which was revealed to Israel alone. What is more, the Written Law enunciates only the general principles of the law, while the Oral Law discusses the specifics of the law. The Written Law is brief, while the Oral Law is lengthy, as it is written: The measure…’ Context and connection to Peri Tzadik: In Peri Tzadik, Bereshit 9, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3) to illuminate his exposition here (“as written (Tanchuma, Noach 3), and it is what shines from the supernal crown of the letter Yod which hints to Ayin (Nothingness), as written (Zohar Part III, 65b) unto the letter Yod which...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the inner dimensions of Torah and divine service developed in Peri Tzadik.
column13: Wherefore the Torah repeatedly commands the love of the convert (Bava Metzia 59b). column15: “And Isaac sowed in that land, and found in that same year a hundredfold, and the Lord blessed him” (Genesis 26:12). My grandfather (the Beit Yaakov) taught that the attribute of Isaac is sowing (zeri’ah): when a seed is planted in the ground, to the outward eye it appears to rot and dissolve completely, yet precisely from that dissolution springs forth a hundredfold harvest. So too, every contraction and humbling that a person undergoes in divine service is a sowing that yields manifold spiritual growth.

The meaning of this is: every generation clearly perceives that the generation preceding it acted as an intermediary bridge between the Blessed Name and itself;Connection (editorial): Contextual connection (editorial): This passage is included as a broader conceptual comparison from the second tradition. column13: “This is also why the years of Creation are counted from Tishrei, corresponding to the level of primordial thought according to which Israel sanctifies the times. Thus the lunar conjunctions, which determine the lunar months, are calculated from the traditional epoch of BeHaRaD, following the view that the world was created in Tishrei, as is known from the calculations of intercalation. The solar seasons, however, are counted from Nisan, because that is when Creation became manifest in the realm of action: the moon receives from the sun, and the power of the sun becomes operative. Israel were given that month in order to sanctify the moon. In primordial thought the moon too was a great light, as it will again be in the future, when from the perspective of that thought the two luminaries are both great. Only in the realm of action was the moon diminished, because in this world “one who eats what is not his own is ashamed.” Awe is itself identified with this holy shame, and this is the quality of Israel—who are characterized by bashfulness—which is absent from the nations. Through this very diminishment, Israel sanctify the appointed times. In the Oral Torah the central sanctification is therefore fixed in Tishrei, on Rosh Hashanah, for Israel’s unique power is that their sanctity can reach all the way to the root of Divine thought. They therefore count the lunar year from Tishrei, corresponding to the thought in which both luminaries are great. This is the entire wisdom of the sages of Israel in the Oral Torah: to cleave to His wisdom and His thought, through which their own wisdom itself becomes Torah. This is not so with the sages of the nations. Their wisdom can recognize that one thing is evil and another good, but they believe that evil, once present, has no rectification; such is the conclusion of unaided wisdom. Thus the Midrash teaches that when Wisdom was asked what should happen to the sinner, it answered, “Evil pursues sinners.” Therefore they count the Flood from Nisan. According to their understanding, even under strict justice there could have been no alternative to the Flood, for sin necessarily draws punishment after it. They believe that a being cannot truly change from what it is. Thus Balaam did not change even though he knew that his path represented the ultimate evil.”
column15: 1–47:end.Extended English quotation from Akiva interlinear: And this underlies the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua ( Rosh Hashanah 11a ): Rabbi Eliezer held that the world was created in Tishrei, whereas Rabbi Yehoshua held that the world was created in Nisan. And their dispute centers on these verses: Rabbi Eliezer expounded: “And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree”—which month is it when the earth puts forth grasses and trees are laden with ripe fruit? You must say: this is Tishrei. And Rabbi Yehoshua says: From where do we know that in Nisan the world was created? … [excerpt continues]Connection (editorial): Contextual connection (editorial): This passage is included as a broader conceptual comparison from the second tradition. column13: “… resembling the months of the moon, each of which in its own right constitutes a full, complete cycle comparable to its fellow. Nonetheless, the duration of the nights in which the moon serves changes in accordance with the variations in the position of the sun during its annual path, which itself is an apparent shift dependent upon the terrestrial recipients, as has been explained. And in the month of Nisan the divine letters are aligned in their direct order (Y-H-V-H), for during that month the spiritual perception descends directly from Hashem, Who raised you from Egypt: 'In Nisan they were redeemed, and in Nisan they are destined to be redeemed, etc.,' wherein Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehudah disputed (Rosh Hashanah 11a), …”

column13: “On the fourth day He created the sun and the moon, and in the future He will exact punishment from those who worship them. The creation of the luminaries to illuminate the world parallels the giving of the Torah, which shone the light of Torah upon all who enter the world. Our Sages of blessed memory taught (Shabbat 89b) that Mount Sinai was so named because hatred descended there upon the idolatrous nations, through the attribute of victory, the level of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, whose face was like the face of the sun (Bava Batra 75a). Our Sages of blessed memory also taught (Nedarim 8b) that in the future there will be no Gehinnom; rather, the sun will be removed from its sheath—the righteous, etc., and the wicked, etc. This follows the principle: 'The righteous shall walk in them, while sinners shall stumble in them.' Likewise, they taught (Shabbat 88b) that for those who turn to the left in Torah it becomes a potion of death; 'evil pursues sinners,' for the sin itself becomes the punishment. This is the meaning of the statement (Bava Batra 16a): he is the evil inclination; he is the Angel of Death.”

column14: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 8:6
column15: And akin to what is brought in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 34): If you see a male running after a female—accept it; and if you see a female running after a male—do not accept it. Meaning: if you see that the male exerts dominion over the female—accept it, for so Hashem established in the world; and if you see a female running after the male—do not accept it, because this is the reverse of the natural law established by Hashem in the world, that the male govern over the female.
